blocks.title: Three areas
blocks.html: The screen has three areas: the toolbar along the top, the layer panel on the left and the map in the centre. Almost every support call starts by asking the user which of the three they are looking at.

blocks.title: Who sees what
blocks.html: The layers listed in the panel depend on the groups the user belongs to. Two people on the same screen can see different layer lists, and that is expected.

questions.prompt: A user says a layer is missing from the panel, but a colleague can see it. What is the most likely cause?
options: The two users are in different groups
questions.explanation: The layer list is filtered by group permissions.

blocks.title: Moving around
blocks.html: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. The zoom to extent button brings the whole city back into view, which is the quickest way out when a user is lost over an empty area.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence.
questions.cloze: When the user is lost over an empty area, use _____ to bring the city back.
questions.explanation: When the user is lost over an empty area, use zoom to extent to bring the city back.

questions.prompt: Which action pans the map?
questions.explanation: Dragging pans; scrolling zooms.

blocks.title: Search box
blocks.html:
The search box accepts a street address or a parcel code. Results are pinned on the map; clicking the pin opens the parcel.

  • Start with the street name, then the number.
  • Parcel codes are searched exactly.

questions.prompt: Which toolbar button is highlighted in this screenshot?
questions.explanation: The first button opens the search box.

blocks.title: Visibility
blocks.html: Tick a layer in the panel to draw it. Some layers only draw below a certain scale: if a ticked layer does not appear, ask the user to zoom in before opening a ticket.

questions.prompt: A ticked layer does not draw. What do you ask first?
questions.explanation: Many layers have a minimum scale and only draw when zoomed in.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence.
questions.cloze: Layers that only draw below a certain _____ look missing when zoomed out.
questions.explanation: Layers that only draw below a certain scale look missing when zoomed out.

blocks.title: Identify
blocks.html: Clicking a feature with the identify tool lists its attributes. If nothing is listed, the click probably hit an area with no feature.

blocks.title: Measure
blocks.html: The measure tool draws a line or an area and shows the length in metres. Double-click to finish.

questions.prompt: How does the user finish a measurement?
questions.explanation: A double-click closes the line or area.

questions.prompt: Where is the list of layers?
questions.explanation: Layers live in the left panel.

questions.prompt: What does zoom to extent do?
questions.explanation: It zooms back to the full city extent.

questions.prompt: The identify tool shows nothing after a click. Most likely?
questions.explanation: An empty identify result usually means the click hit no feature.

blocks.title: The pencil
blocks.html: Select a layer in the panel and press the pencil. The button stays grey when the user's group can view the layer but not edit it.

questions.prompt: The pencil is grey for one layer only. Why?
options: The layer is view-only for the user's group
The map is too far out
questions.explanation: Edit rights are granted per layer and per group.

blocks.title: Vertex by vertex
blocks.html: Click to add each vertex and double-click to close the polygon. The attribute form opens as soon as the polygon is closed.

questions.prompt: When does the attribute form open?
questions.explanation: Closing the polygon opens the form.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence.
questions.explanation: A double-click closes the polygon.

blocks.title: Why snap
blocks.html: With snapping on, a new vertex jumps to the nearest existing vertex. Neighbouring parcels then share the border exactly, with no gaps or slivers.

questions.prompt: What problem does snapping prevent?
questions.explanation: Shared borders stay exact.

blocks.title: Required fields
blocks.html: Fields marked with an asterisk are required; the form will not save while one is empty. Drop-down fields only accept values from their list.

blocks.title: Undo
blocks.html: While drawing, the undo button removes the last vertex, not the whole feature.

questions.prompt: The Save button does nothing. What do you check first?
questions.explanation: An empty required field blocks saving.

questions.prompt: What does undo remove while drawing?
questions.explanation: Undo steps back one vertex.

blocks.title: Commit
blocks.html: Edits stay local until Save is pressed. Closing the session without saving discards them, and the platform asks for confirmation first.

questions.prompt: A user lost an afternoon of edits. What most likely happened?
options: The session was closed without saving
questions.explanation: Edits are only stored when Save is pressed.

blocks.title: Groups, not people
blocks.html: Permissions are granted to groups; users inherit them by membership. To give someone access, add them to the right group instead of granting rights one by one.

questions.prompt: How should access be granted to a new analyst?
options: Layer by layer to the user
By adding the user to a group
questions.explanation: Groups keep permissions consistent and auditable.

blocks.title: View and edit
blocks.html: Each group gets view and/or edit per layer. Edit without view is not allowed: the screen grants view automatically.

questions.prompt: Can a group edit a layer it cannot view?
questions.explanation: Edit always comes with view.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence.
questions.cloze: Permissions are granted per layer and per _____.
questions.explanation: Permissions are granted per layer and per group.

blocks.title: Who changed what
blocks.html: The audit log records every insert, update and delete with the user and the time. Filter by layer first; then by user or by date.

questions.prompt: What is the best first filter when investigating a changed parcel?
questions.explanation: Filtering by layer narrows the log the fastest.

questions.prompt: Where do users get their permissions from?
questions.explanation: Permissions are inherited from groups.

questions.prompt: What does the audit log record?
questions.explanation: Every data change is logged.
